messages:
alex: Heads-up — seeing p99 latency jumps and SLO misses on rl-model-v2 in us-west-2 for the last 10m. Alert text: "continuous batching pressure -> max_batch hits". p50 fine, p95 ~230ms, p99 ~1.2s, queue length ~300. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/shot/abc123 :alarm:
mira: I can confirm. GPU util ~94% across the pool but batcher reports lots of partial/short batches. Admission controller admits aggressively but max_batch_size per-shard is 16 so we get many small dispatches -> higher tail.
jordan: That matches the change we rolled last week (packing-cap tweak). I think some shards still have old kernel/packing mismatch. Could be packing admission admits requests that can't be merged because of token distribution.
priya: Bumping max_batch_size will reduce number of dispatches but increases per-dispatch mem usage. Tradeoff: lower per-token cost and lower avg latency vs risk of OOM on long sequences.
alex: Quick diagnostic ideas: 1) check batcher.admit metrics (`batch_wait_ms`, `partial_batch_pct`) 2) check per-shard `max_batch_size` and `kernel_variant` 3) look for socket TX drops on pod NICs (net backpressure). Anyone want to take a canary change?
mira: I can run a canary in us-west-2a. Plan: increase `max_batch_size` from 16 -> 32 only for rl-model-v2 pool in that AZ and watch p99 + GPU mem.
jordan: Also add an admission rule: when queue_length > 200, throttle low-priority tenants (route tags) to preserve SLO for high-priority routes. That should buy headroom without global config change.
priya: Agreed. Also enable a short-term KV-cache spillover for hot prefixes to reduce re-computation; that will lower batch pressure for repeated prompts.
alex: Command we can run (runtime CLI):
```
redwoodctl runtime update --pool rl-model-v2 --az us-west-2a --set max_batch_size=32 --canary 1m
```
I'll hand off to mira to execute.
mira: Running canary now. Starting: `redwoodctl` output: "canary update started (1/5 shards)". Will post results in ~10m.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiated by mira on rl-model-v2 us-west-2a. Rollout ID: r-20260318-33. Monitoring: 20m.
jordan: While canary runs, let's add a temporary admission rule in the controller config (non-breaking):
```
admission:
  queue_threshold: 200
  low_priority_limit: 100
  action: throttle
```
This will keep the inflight low-priority slots bounded.
priya: Note on cost: if canary is stable and we flip pool-wide to 32, throughput should increase and per-token cost drop ~7-12% for this workload. But watch for increased OOM risk on mixed long-seq traffic.
alex: Mira, once canary hits steady state (p95/p99 improvement or stable), roll to remaining AZs. If p99 gets worse, immediately revert to 16 and re-enable packing-cap conservative mode.
mira: Canary results after 12m: p95 down 15%, p99 down 200ms -> now ~1.0s, queue length down to ~90 from 300. GPU mem headroom OK on canary shards (peak 86%). Moving to roll to other AZs in 10m.
jordan: Great. Also opened a ticket to fix packing-admission mismatch: TICKET-4309 — investigate why packing-cap and kernel_variant drifted across shard configs.
priya: Will monitor cost delta and long-seq tail. Also adding a regression alert on `partial_batch_pct` rise > 20%.
alex: Final plan recorded: (1) roll max_batch_size=32 to whole pool (2) add admission-rule for low-priority throttle (3) short-term KV spillover ON (4) ticket TICKET-4309 for root cause. Reopen if we see p99 > 1.5s.
mira: Rolling to remaining AZs now. Will post final numbers once done.
jordan: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rollout completed across us-west-2 for rl-model-v2. Rollout ID: r-20260318-33. Health: green. Metrics: p95 -18%, p99 -0.18s (stable).
